items.title: Anthropic: Claude Mythos 5 designs quantum circuits beating published ones, up to 17x fewer gates
items.summary: In an Anthropic STEM Fellows project with Harvard and QuEra collaborators (arXiv 2610.22367), Claude Mythos 5 improved on the best published circuits on all eight tasks given. A 53-hour autonomous run produced an elliptic-curve point-addition design using 12% more qubits than the smallest prior design but 17x fewer gates; for Decoded Quantum Interferometry it swapped in Berlekamp-Massey decoding, cutting decoder gates about 12x versus Google's prior construction. These are resource-estimate gains, not hardware runs.
items.why_it_matters: It points to AI agents finding algorithmic improvements relevant to the cost of attacking elliptic-curve cryptography, though only in circuit estimates.

items.title: Anthropic says Claude traced NIST ECDSA curve seeds to a 1990s C random generator in under 30 minutes
items.summary: Anthropic reports Claude worked out that the seeds for NIST P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521 were not hash outputs but lrand48 output seeded with a Unix timestamp (P-256: 1997-08-16 01:52:34). It recovered hidden state by brute force for four seeds and used LLL lattice reduction for the truncated-output prime-curve seeds, and explained six base points as coming from the FreeLIP generator; other base points and the B-163 seed remain unexplained. Anthropic says this is not a cryptographic break but makes a deliberate backdoor far less plausible, and will donate the $36,864 bounty to the Internet Security Research Group.
items.why_it_matters: It speaks to a 25-year suspicion about the NIST curve seeds and is a concrete example of an AI model doing open-ended cryptographic archaeology.
